pairs: Filius sapiens lætificat patrem,
A wise son gladdens the father.
filius vero stultus mœstitia est matris suæ.
Yet truly, a foolish son is the grief of his mother.
Nil proderunt thesauri impietatis,
Treasures of impiety will profit nothing.
justitia vero liberabit a morte.
Truly, justice shall liberate from death.
Non affliget Dominus fame animam justi,
The Lord will not afflict with famine the soul of the just,
et insidias impiorum subvertet.
and he will overthrow the treacheries of the impious.
Egestatem operata est manus remissa;
The neglectful hand has wrought destitution.
manus autem fortium divitias parat.
But the hand of the steadfast prepares riches.
Qui nititur mendaciis,
He who advances by lies,
hic pascit ventos;
this one feeds on the wind.
idem autem ipse sequitur aves volantes.
For he is the same as one who runs after flying birds.
Qui congregat in messe, filius sapiens est;
He who gathers the harvest is a wise son.
qui autem stertit æstate, filius confusionis.
But he who snores in warm weather is a son of confusion.
Benedictio Domini super caput justi;
The blessing of the Lord is on the head of the just.
os autem impiorum operit iniquitas.
But iniquity covers the mouth of the impious.
Memoria justi cum laudibus,
The remembrance of the just is with praises.
et nomen impiorum putrescet.
And the name of the impious shall decay.
Sapiens corde præcepta suscipit;
The wise of heart accept precepts.
stultus cæditur labiis.
The foolish are cut down by the lips.
Qui ambulat simpliciter ambulat confidenter;
He who walks in simplicity walks in confidence.
qui autem depravat vias suas manifestus erit.
But he who corrupts his ways shall be discovered.
Qui annuit oculo dabit dolorem;
He who winks with the eye gives sorrow.
et stultus labiis verberabitur.
And the foolish in lips shall be beaten.
Vena vitæ os justi,
The mouth of the just is a vein of life.
et os impiorum operit iniquitatem.
And the mouth of the impious covers iniquity.
Odium suscitat rixas,
Hatred rises up from disputes.
et universa delicta operit caritas.
And charity covers all offenses.
In labiis sapientis invenitur sapientia,
In the lips of the wise, wisdom is discovered.
et virga in dorso ejus qui indiget corde.
And a rod is for the back of one who lacks heart.
Sapientes abscondunt scientiam;
The wise store away knowledge.
os autem stulti confusioni proximum est.
But the mouth of the foolish is a neighbor to confusion.
Substantia divitis, urbs fortitudinis ejus;
The substance of the rich is the city of his strength.
pavor pauperum egestas eorum.
The fear of the poor is their destitution.
Opus justi ad vitam,
The work of the just is unto life.
fructus autem impii ad peccatum.
But the fruit of the impious is unto sin.
Via vitæ custodienti disciplinam;
The way of life is for those who observe discipline.
qui autem increpationes relinquit, errat.
But whoever abandons correction wanders astray.
Abscondunt odium labia mendacia;
Lying lips conceal hatred;
qui profert contumeliam, insipiens est.
whoever brings forth contempt is unwise.
In multiloquio non deerit peccatum,
In a multitude of speaking, sin will not be lacking.
qui autem moderatur labia sua prudentissimus est.
But whoever tempers his lips is most prudent.
Argentum electum lingua justi;
The tongue of the just is choice silver.
cor autem impiorum pro nihilo.
But the heart of the impious is exchanged for nothing.
Labia justi erudiunt plurimos;
The lips of the just instruct many.
qui autem indocti sunt in cordis egestate morientur.
But those who are unlearned shall die in destitution of heart.
Benedictio Domini divites facit,
The blessing of the Lord causes riches.
nec sociabitur eis afflictio.
Affliction will not be a companion to them.
Quasi per risum stultus operatur scelus,
The foolish work wickedness as if in jest.
sapientia autem est viro prudentia.
But wisdom is prudence to a man.
Quod timet impius veniet super eum;
What the impious fear will overwhelm them.
desiderium suum justus dabitur.
The just shall be given their desire.
Quasi tempestas transiens non erit impius;
Like a passing tempest, so the impious one will be no more.
justus autem quasi fundamentum sempiternum.
But the just one is like an everlasting foundation.
Sicut acetum dentibus,
Like vinegar to the teeth,
et fumus oculis,
and smoke to the eyes,
sic piger his qui miserunt eum.
so is a lazy one to those who sent him.
Timor Domini apponet dies,
The fear of the Lord adds days.
et anni impiorum breviabuntur.
And the years of the impious will be shortened.
Exspectatio justorum lætitia,
The expectation of the just is rejoicing.
spes autem impiorum peribit.
But the hope of the impious will perish.
Fortitudo simplicis via Domini,
The strength of the simple is the way of the Lord,
et pavor his qui operantur malum.
and it is fear to those who work evil.
Justus in æternum non commovebitur,
The just in eternity shall not be moved.
impii autem non habitabunt super terram.
But the impious will not live upon the earth.
Os justi parturiet sapientiam;
The mouth of the just shall bring forth wisdom.
lingua pravorum peribit.
The tongue of the depraved will perish.
Labia justi considerant placita,
The lips of the just consider what is acceptable.
et os impiorum perversa.
And the mouth of the impious considers perversities.
